key_insight: LOKI discovers row-level join paths between disjoint tables by using sentences as evidence, turning implicit text/table links into explicit, typed integrations.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to integrate data-lake tables that lack schemas or keys, enabling provenance-aware joins without requiring manual row links or expensive prompting.
method: Horizontal bidirectional cross-attention learns contextualized row and sentence representations.
A global table-text contrastive objective surfaces fine-grained row-sentence associations without local labels.
Discovered associations are grouped into relation-consistent join paths and materialized as typed tables with sentence provenance.
evidence_signal: On real-world benchmarks, the method outperformed state-of-the-art multi-modal discovery approaches and achieved 0.982 macro typed-pair precision while reducing LLM API cost by up to 40× versus direct prompting.
watch_item: Performance depends on useful textual evidence being present, and the pipeline may be more complex to deploy than simpler retrieval or schema-matching methods.
paper_title: Discovery-Driven Integration of Disjoint Tables via Text
